title: US sees highest number of measles cases in 35 years
snippet:
# US measles cases reach 35-year high

Getty Images A fact sheet for measles sits on a table with a dark blue tablecloth, in a clipboard

The US has hit a 35-year high in measles cases, according to new figures from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The US has seen 2,318 confirmed cases of measles in 2026, just seven months into the year, up from last year's high of 2,289, when two unvaccinated children died of the disease. [...] Earlier this year, a federal judge blocked the US government from implementing a series of sweeping changes to childhood immunisations under Kennedy's leadership, including slashing the number of recommended shots for children from 17 to 11.

To achieve herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects the unvaccinated, around 95% of the population must have the shots. But vaccination rates have dipped far below that in some areas. [...] The rising number of cases have come as vaccine hesitancy in the US has increased in recent years, leading to lower immunisation rates.

In November, a panel is set to decide whether the US will lose its status of having eliminated measles, which Canada lost last year.

A country loses elimination status after a year or more of continuous transmission of the same strain of the measles virus.

title: US measles cases reach 35-year high, for second record-breaking year in a row
snippet:
“Measles outbreaks are very labor-intensive, just given how quickly it can spread,” said Meredith Robinson, vaccine-preventable diseases coordinator for the Virginia Department of Health.

Virginia had a few sporadic measles cases at the start of 2026, related to international travel or travel to areas of the US with an outbreak. But vaccination rates in the state are high, Robinson said, so those cases didn’t appear to spread. [...] The total number of measles cases in 2026 has already surpassed last year’s total, according to data posted by the CDC on Friday. At least 2,318 cases have been reported with more than five months left in the year. [...] Measles has continued its historic resurgence in the United States this year, with a second record-breaking year in a row. Just over halfway through 2026, the country has recorded more cases than in any other year since 1991 – surpassing a grim milestone that was just topped last year.

The disease was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, but more cases have been recorded in the past 18 months than there have been in the previous 25 years combined.

title: US measles cases hit 35-year high as vaccinations decline
snippet:
As many as 93% of this year's cases were in ​unvaccinated individuals, with a fraction ⁠of the rest having received one or two doses of vaccine before being infected, the CDC said.

Infections were documented by the CDC this year in 45 states and the District of Columbia, with 93% associated with one of 35 new outbreaks reported in 2026, versus 48 last year. [...] "Since early last year, federal leaders have dismissed measles as benign and unavoidable and have spread misleading information about the MMR vaccine," said Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

"Halfway into 2026, the U.S. is experiencing the worst year for ​measles since 1991. We are witnessing an avoidable crisis that disproportionately hurts children." [...] The overall 2026 figures represent ‌the highest number of U.S. cases in a single year since a major resurgence of the highly contagious disease in the period from 1989 to 1991, with more than 55,000 infections and 123 deaths.
